newsitem.title: UK: Hotels business boost Lonrho year results.
newsitem.headline: Hotels business boost Lonrho year results.

text.p: Widely diversified conglomerate Lonrho Plc, which is in the throes of a company split-up, on Thursday reported a 12.6 percent in full-year pretax profits and said talks to sell its Princess hotels are progressing.

The company said it remains committed to breaking up its mining and non-mining business. "We believe that shareholders will obtain the greatest benefit from a demerger or a combination of a sale and demerger," chief executive Nick Morrell said in a statement.
Lonrho, in which South Africa's Anglo American Corp has a 28 percent stake, said full-year pre-tax profit before exceptional items rose to 170 million pounds ($284.5 million) from 151 million.

The results were boosted by improved performances of the hotels, the agricultural and other other trading operations. But the profit rise, which was bigger than analysts' had expected, was dampened by lower mining results, which were hit by falling mineral prices and devaluation of the rand, Lonrho said.

The group's sale of its Metropole hotels to Stakis Plc led to an exceptional charge of 87 million pounds. The Metropole chain was sold in October and Lonrho said at the time it expected to conclude the sale of its Princess hotels the following month. The hotel sales are part of Lonrho's plan, announced a year ago, to streamline its wide spread of businesses. The split of the mining and trading business would be the most ambitious part of that plan.

But the demerger is believed to be delayed by an EU investigation into the competition implications of Anglo's stake in Lonrho. Both firms are among the three leading producers of platinum, which is used in car exhaust catalysts.
Lonrho shares were indicated 1/2 penny higher at 125-1/2 pence in pre-market trading. ($1=.5976 Pound)
